climate_pressure: Rising temperature, longer dry spells and inadequate water.
documented_impact: Reduced rain-fed agricultural performance and livelihood security.
fcv_mediator: Debt, landlessness risk, rising input costs, declining credit, poverty and an existing armed-conflict environment.
possible_consequence: These combined pressures may influence grievances and household/community relationships with armed resistance actors; the evidence does not show climate as an independent cause of recruitment or violence.
geographies: Magway and lower Sagaing Dry Zone
uncertainty: SIPRI/NUPI directly presents the chain but does not estimate the independent effect of climate stress. (SIPRI6)
resilience_factors: climate information and local conflict-sensitive agricultural support
compact_statement: Dry Zone climate stress can worsen farm hardship, but any effect on conflict dynamics is mediated through finance, livelihoods and pre-existing political violence.

documented_impact: Damage to shelter, WASH, infrastructure, livelihoods and services.
fcv_mediator: Humanitarian-access restrictions, insecurity, territorial contestation and blocked transport.
possible_consequence: Slower relief and recovery can prolong unmet needs and deepen vulnerability.
affected_groups: Rohingya and ethnic Rakhine populations among others
alternative_explanations: terrain and the scale of the disaster
uncertainty: Evidence is strong for specific events but cannot be assumed uniform across Myanmar. (Doctors Without Borders4)
compact_statement: Conflict and access restrictions have demonstrably reduced the reach of climate-disaster response in specific Myanmar settings.

documented_impact: Temporary relocation, camp damage, WASH shortages and mine/ERW uncertainty.
fcv_mediator: Prior conflict displacement and settlement in vulnerable locations.
possible_consequence: People displaced by conflict may face repeated displacement and accumulating asset/service losses during climatic disasters.
alternative_explanations: poor settlement siting and inadequate infrastructure can generate vulnerability independently of conflict
uncertainty: National IDP figures do not indicate how many IDPs are directly climate-exposed. (World Bank5)
compact_statement: Conflict displacement can turn a climatic shock into repeated displacement and additional protection risk.

climate_pressure: Floods, cyclones, heat and other weather extremes.
documented_impact: Need to evacuate, migrate or relocate.
fcv_mediator: Conflict, mobility restrictions, insecurity and contested territory.
possible_consequence: Households unable to move safely may remain in highly exposed areas or lose access to livelihoods and assistance.
geographies: source emphasizes displaced and minority populations
uncertainty: Limited quantitative evidence identifies the relative contribution of each mobility constraint. (SIPRI6)
compact_statement: Conflict-related mobility constraints can reduce people's ability to use migration or evacuation as climate coping strategies.

fcv_mediator: Competing authorities' attempts to demonstrate governing capacity and legitimacy.
possible_consequence: Disaster response may reshape grievances and perceived authority without the hazard itself causing renewed conflict.
affected_groups: Disaster-affected communities including marginalized Rohingya populations
institutions: KNU and other local governance actors
uncertainty: Political effects vary strongly by actor and locality. (SIPRI6)
compact_statement: In post-coup Myanmar, disaster and climate action can become part of struggles over authority rather than merely technical adaptation.

climate_pressure: Climate hazards interacting with seasonal farming needs.
documented_impact: Threats to harvest and food security.
fcv_mediator: Armed confrontation preventing normal agricultural activity.
possible_consequence: Negotiated agricultural access may create a temporary peace-supporting window.
alternative_explanations: military or political rather than climate-specific
uncertainty: No evidence of durable peace effects. (SIPRI6)
compact_statement: Locally mediated harvest access can support food security and temporary de-escalation, but it is not evidence that adaptation causes peace.

climate_pressure: Multi-hazard climate risk requiring information, planning and coordinated adaptation.
documented_impact: High demand for climate information, agricultural adaptation and disaster preparedness.
fcv_mediator: Fragmented territorial control, contested institutions and politicization of environmental action.
possible_consequence: National adaptation plans and services may have uneven territorial reach and may be interpreted through political competition.
alternative_explanations: Long-standing administrative capacity and finance constraints predate the coup
uncertainty: No national post-2021 implementation audit was located.
compact_statement: Conflict and divided authority appear to make adaptation capacity territorially uneven and politically contested.

documented_impact: Local infrastructure, food and service needs.
fcv_mediator: Weak/contested state reach and security conditions.
possible_consequence: Community assets, grassroots institutions and third-party implementation may sustain limited resilience where conventional public delivery is constrained.
geographies: Karen areas and conflict-affected World Bank project locations
alternative_explanations: Selection toward more stable areas may itself explain better delivery
uncertainty: Programme outputs and institutional activity are not evidence of durable resilience or peace outcomes. (World Food Programme3)
compact_statement: Alternative delivery institutions can bridge some resilience gaps, but effectiveness and equity require independent evaluation.
